headline.label: false alarms, fixed cutoff, large camera bump (V-JEPA 2)
AUROC: failure detection is near chance on this task

intro: What the real data says, plainly. (1) The promise can break: a large camera bump pushed the fixed cutoff to 38% false alarms with V-JEPA 2 and 71% with SigLIP 2, against a 10% target; the adaptive cutoff stayed at 4–12.5% on every model and shift. Smaller shifts mostly didn't break it. (2) The bigger problem: on this task, at 2 frames/s with 25 training demos, no model separates failures from successes well (AUROC 0.41–0.61). An alarm that holds its false-alarm promise but can't see failures isn't useful yet. (3) Conditioning on actions added nothing measurable. These are the things to fix before the physical experiment: more training data, a higher frame rate, and a task where failures are visible.

footer: Setup: ArmnetBench v0.1, task “Put the eye drops into the basket”, front camera at 2 fps; world model trained on 25 human teleop demos, calibrated on 25 more (experiment A) or on 55 successful policy runs (B); B test set 70 policy runs (k = 15 used by recalibration, 55 scored: 24 successes, 31 failures). Five frozen encoders, CPU, Vercel Sandbox, Nov 6 2026. Full outputs (per-episode scores, all tables, logs): results.tgz. Note: the demo clips show the score dropping back ~2 s after the bump because the predictor adapts to the new view, so a mid-run bump is caught but a bump before the run starts is harder.
